LIVERPOOL SUMMER- ASSIZES,, 1890. The Commissions for holding these Assizes will be opened on SATURDAY, the 26th,July, at 11 o'clock a.m., and the trials will be proceeded with immediately afterwards. The Prosecutors and Witnesses in the after-mentioned cases are required to be in attendance at the times specified in the following List, and not earlier, and on all subsequent days, at the sitting of the Court ; and the trials are to proceed in the order in which the cases are arranged in the List, unless the Court shall otherwise direct, viz. On SATURDAY, the 26th July, at 11 o'clock a.m. The QUEEN V. Lewis Williams, burglary ; Luis Izenstein, burglary ; Edwin Jones and others, burglary, do.; William Hawkins, burglary; Mary Jane Burke, wounding; Mary Friel, manslaughter ; John Minton, burglary; Patrick Hackett and others, burglary ; James Cohen, robbery; Ben- jamin Novell°, manslaughter ; William Yates and others, robbery ; James Osborne, burglary ; Michael Carroll and another, robbery, &c.; William Mitchard, robbery ; Joseph Matthews, wounding ; Mary O'Neill and another, manslaugh- ter ; Catherine McLean, burglary; William Thomas and others, burglary ; William Whalen, wounding ; Thomas Baxendale and others, burglary ; Eliza Langley, bigamy; John Shaugh- nessy and another, shopbreaking and larceny ; Walter John- son, Mint case. On MONDAY, the 28th July, at 10.30 a.m. The QUEEN V. Peter Schonberg, rape; John Molyneux, at- tempting to carnally know a girl above 13 and under 16 ; James Rimmer, attempting to carnally know a girl under 13: William Roberts, carnally knowing a girl above 13 and under 16 ;John Corrigan, perjury; John Lomas, carnally knowing a girl above 13 and under 16 ; Eric Granger, libel ; James Donoghue, wounding ; Edward William Vaughan, man- slaughter ; Dennis James Woods, attempting to murder; Leah Charlton, murder ; John Duckworth Pickavance and, another, murder ; Patrick Ready and another, robbery; John Thomas Hough, carnally knowing a girl under 13 ; Rebecca McDonald, attempting to murder; Edward Bond. rape; Martin Burns, attempting to carnally know a girl above 13 and under 16. And all other cases. The foregoing regulations will be strictly enforced, and persons making default in the observance of them will he liable to have their costs disallowed. HERBERT STEPHEN. Clerk of Assize. Office of Clerk of Assize, Preston, 22nd July, 1890. N.B.—lt is particularly requested that all Depositions, Inquisitions, and Recognisances may be IMMEDIATELY for- warded to me, at Preston.

DROWNING ACCIDENTS. A boat containing three shop assistants was capsized off Chathatn, on Wednesday night, and one of the occup- ants was drowned. Three similar accidents have occur- red this week near the same place. The fishing smack Sarah, of Howth, was run down by a drawler on Wednesday evening off the Skerries, aud three men on board were drowned. TEPRIBLE PRACTICAL JOKE. __- TWENTY MEN DROWNED. NEW Ironic, THURSDAY.—Last night a man, name un- known, thinking it would be a good joke to set adrift a raft which was fastened to the bank at Pembroke, Ontario, cut the rope which held it. The raft rapidly drifted, was caught in the rapids, and knocked to pieces. Of the twenty-two men on the raft at the time, twenty were drowned.

MR. JOSEPH ARCIL At a meeting of delegates of the North-West Norfolk Liberal Association, on Tuesday morning, Mr. Joseph Arch was unanimously adopted as candidate at the next election. • DEATH OP MISS LYDIA BECKER. A telegram was received in Manchester, on Saturday, announcing the death, at Geneva, on Friday night, of Miss Lydia Becker, who had gone there in the hope of obtaining relief from an attack of diphtheria. Miss Becker had for many years been a leading figure in the agitation for women's suffrage, to which movement, in- deed, she dedicated the chief share of her time. She was concerned also in all the movements for the recognition of women's rights and for the improvement of the status of her sex. For a long time she had edited the "Women's Suffrage Journal," and the Manchester National Sdciety for Women Suffrage was chiefly directed by her. Miss Becker took a considerable share of the public work of Manchester, and was a member of the School Board from its foundation.
